data.text:
Approve gated command 'claim.force' for agent sw-quotameters?

data.note: P-swarm push lane: quota meters per item body, UNAVAILABLE never zero [operator approval Q606e555f9c by policy:claim_unavailable via policy]

data.summary: The rule is documented as covering an item held by a vanished/unavailable holder, but its predicate in services/approvals/policy.py is _true. A plain agent claim of a dep-blocked item with no holder (B-quota-meters, no force, no approval passed) was refused by plan_blocker, then re-run forced by _claim_by_approval through Q606e555f9c approved by policy:claim_unavailable, human:false. The claim@1 reply carries no field saying it was forced or approved; only the lease note and ask events show it. So next says blocked, claim grants a worktree, and the agent cannot tell. Expected: the predicate requires a lapsed lease whose holder is gone, and any forced grant is stated in the claim reply.
data.title: Standing rule claim_unavailable approves any claim.force, so a plain claim silently passes unmet dependencies

data.claim: Vendor percent comes from three sources with different scales; Claude transcripts repeat (message.id, requestId) with identical usage; Kilo session columns default to 0 and count whole lifetimes, so only message rows give a window, and a zero there or a zero cost means not recorded.
data.falsifier: Kilo all-zero sessions turn out to have nonzero message tokens, or session columns match message sums over a window, or duplicate Claude keys carry different usage.
data.mechanism: Kilo columns are DEFAULT 0 NOT NULL, so absence is stored as 0. A session touched in a window carries its lifetime total. Claude writes one transcript line per content block, each with the message usage.
data.probe: python3 over [REDACTED:path] cachedUsageUtilization (numbers only), 48 ddflow transcripts, read-only kilo.db aggregates over 5h and 168h; statusline docs; strings of claude 2.1.318
data.probe_output: cache: utilization 0-100, resets_at ISO, fetchedAtMs 320h old, resets long past. statusline docs: used_percentage 0-100, resets_at Unix epoch seconds, both windows in rate_limits. binary schema: rate_limit_info status, resetsAt int, rateLimitType, utilization; no real event on this machine, so the 0-1 scale rests on the item body and R-usage-quota only. transcripts: 1419 keys, 0 with differing usage, 0 missing a key, 0 without usage, 0 across files; one file 80 of 106 keys repeated. corpus 1.28 GB, 391 MB touched in 7d, 31 MB in 5h. kilo: 3810 sessions, 2316 all-zero tokens, 3786 cost 0; sampled zero sessions hold 0 or 1 zero assistant message. 5h window: session columns 371369056 input, messages 226823205; 168h 18329226113 vs 18310997569; message query 1.9 s on a 13.9 GB db; cost 0 everywhere.

chunk_findings.detail: The `_subset` validator accepts a list with duplicate entries: `ok = isinstance(value, list) and bool(value) and all(v in allowed for v in value)` never checks `len(value) == len(set(value))`. Given a config `token_fields = ["input", "input"]`, validation passes, but the meter that sums token kinds will add the input token count twice, producing an inflated usage total (or for duplicate `token_windows`, duplicate windows in a downstream accumulation). This is a concrete input that makes the reading wrong: the configured selection no longer represents "which token kinds a reading's total includes" as it does for a unique list, and the check intended to enforce `_subset` fails to prevent it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/quota.py:_subset (also affects token_fields at ~line 82)

chunk_findings.detail: `record` appends to `ctx.samples` without acquiring `locked(ctx.samples)`, while `_trim` takes that lock and replaces the whole file. Interleaving: process A is in `_trim`, has read the old log, and is about to `atomic_write`; process B enters `record`, opens the old `ctx.samples` with `O_APPEND` and writes a new sample; A then renames the trimmed file over the path without B's row. B's sample is silently dropped from the sample log, producing an undercount. The lock is ineffective because only one of the two writers honors it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters.py:record/_trim

chunk_findings.detail: When a registered reader raises, `read_all` appends `B.unavailable(name, "", "", "", reason, ctx.now)` with empty `window`, `unit`, and `harness`. `best` matches only the exact requested `window`/`unit`/`harness`, so for any concrete metric request the failed reader normally covers, that unavailable reading is filtered out and `best` returns `None` even though a reader did run and did cover the metric. `best`'s own contract says `None` means no reader covers it at all; a caller that treats `None` as absence and shows 0 then converts an unreadable meter into a false zero, violating r-no-silent-cost.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters.py:read_all/best

chunk_findings.detail: `is_number` calls `math.isfinite(value)` directly on any `int`, and Python raises `OverflowError` for Python integers larger than the float range, e.g. `is_number(10**400)`. A truthful large token count in `Reading(..., status="ok", value=10**400)` or an out-of-range percent `percent(10**400, 1.0)` therefore crashes the meter read instead of returning an ok reading or refusing the unusable figure as `None`/UNAVAILABLE. This violates the “cannot be taken is UNAVAILABLE, never zero” path by raising on input that should be handled as a non-percent or upheld as a real Python integer.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters_base.py:25

chunk_findings.detail: A truncated/invalid JSON assistant line increments `usage.skipped` but never enters `usage.unmetered`, and `read_claude_tokens` passes `skipped` only as detail. Given a single touched transcript containing one torn assistant line such as `{"type":"assistant", "message":{"usage":{"input_tokens":5`, `transcript_usage` returns `rows=[]`, `unmetered=[]`, `skipped=1`, so `_tokens` sees `total=0` and `unmetered=0` and returns an OK zero token reading. That is a false zero for a turn that was present but could not be read, violating r-no-silent-cost.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters_local.py:_scan / read_claude_tokens / _tokens

chunk_findings.detail: `_breakdown` converts `None` optional token kinds to `0` with `getattr(r, kind) or 0`. If `ctx.token_fields` selects an optional kind such as `cache_read`, and a transcript turn has only `input_tokens` and `output_tokens` (so `TokenRow.cache_read is None`), this turn is not counted in `unmetered`; `_tokens` returns OK 0 for that selected kind. The absent kind means no usable figure and must be unmetered/unavailable, not zero—the module’s own `TokenRow` doc says an exposed-absent kind is `None`, never `0`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters_local.py:_breakdown / _tokens

chunk_findings.detail: For Anthropic transcripts, `usage.input_tokens` is the total input count, and `cache_read_input_tokens`/`cache_creation_input_tokens` are subsets of that total. `_row_of` stores the total as `input` and also stores the cache subsets, and `_tokens` sums every selected field. With the normal `token_fields` set containing `input`, `cache_read`, and `cache_write`, a turn with `input_tokens=100`, `output_tokens=50`, `cache_read_input_tokens=30`, `cache_creation_input_tokens=20` returns 200 tokens instead of 150, a clear overcount.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters_local.py:_tokens / _breakdown

chunk_findings.detail: A `session.started` event whose `e.ts` is malformed is turned into `-1.0` by `clock.epoch(e.ts, default=-1.0)` and then filtered out by `>= start`, so it disappears from every window without being recorded as unmetered. Given one malformed `session.started` event and no valid events, `read_ddflow_sessions` returns an OK reading of `0` sessions rather than `UNAVAILABLE`, even though the log contains a session start that cannot be placed in a window. This is a false zero/undercount.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters_local.py:read_ddflow_sessions

chunk_findings.detail: `cachedUsageUtilization.utilization.<window>.utilization` in `[REDACTED:path]` is a fraction 0-1, not a percent 0-100. With `CACHE_SCALE = 1.0`, a concrete cache like `{"cachedUsageUtilization":{"fetchedAtMs":1729591714382,"accountUuid":"u","utilization":{"five_hour":{"utilization":0.5,"resets_at":"2024-10-22T11:00:00Z"}}}}` produces a reading of `0.5` percent instead of `50.0` percent. This is a 100x undercount for real usage, directly against the “no false zero or undercount” intent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters_vendor.py: CACHE_SCALE / read_claude_cache

chunk_findings.detail: `write_cache` writes `path` without creating its parent directory. The `ctx` helper sets `snapshot` to `tmp / "state" / "vendor.json"` but never creates `tmp/state`, so a natural test setup such as `write_cache(ctx(tmp_path).snapshot, five=50, week=20)` raises `FileNotFoundError` before any meter code runs. The function should create `path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` like `write_transcript` does.
chunk_findings.title: tests/quota_meters_support.py:46

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `assert all(r.status == MB.UNAVAILABLE for r in V.read_claude_cache(ctx(tmp_path)))` is vacuously true when `read_claude_cache` returns an empty list. With this `tmp_path` where no cache file exists, an implementation that returned `[]` would still pass while producing no `UNAVAILABLE` reading for the configured `5h`/`week` windows—the exact silent-cost absence this suite is intended to prevent. The test should assert the returned window set is `{"5h", "week"}` with `UNAVAILABLE`, as the malformed-file test does; the same vacuous `all(...)` form appears for absent/corrupt snapshots in `TestSnapshot.test_no_rate_limits_writes_nothing_never_zero` and `TestSnapshot.test_corrupt_snapshot_is_unavailable_and_a_new_write_heals_it`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_quota_meters.py:test_missing_file_is_unavailable

chunk_findings.detail: `turn()` defaults its transcript row timestamp to the current time (`NOW`), as shown by every other test in this file that calls `turn()` without `at` and expects the row to be counted in the 5h window. This test then sets only the file `mtime` to `NOW - 200 * HOUR`. The file is old by mtime, but the row it contains has an in-window timestamp, so a correct reader that honors the row timestamp would report 116 tokens, not 0. The test asserts `(MB.OK, 0.0)`, blessing a false zero/undercount for a transcript file whose mtime diverges from its row timestamp (for example after copy preserving an old mtime or a clock adjustment). If the implementation ever trusts the row timestamp over mtime, this test fails; as written it locks in the silent undercount that r-no-silent-cost says must not happen.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_quota_meters_local.py:test_transcripts_with_nothing_in_the_window_measure_zero

chunk_findings.detail: A reader that raises is turned into one UNAVAILABLE reading with blank window, unit and harness (`unavailable(name, "", "", "", reason, ctx.now)`). `best` only matches on those three fields, so given Claude token reads raising `OSError` and a caller asking `best(read_all(ctx), "5h", "tokens", "claude")`, the failure row never matches and `best` returns None (“no reader covers it”) instead of UNAVAILABLE. A caller that treats None as no usage records a false zero, which is the silent-cost case this wrapper is supposed to prevent.
chunk_findings.title: `best` / `read_all`

chunk_findings.detail: Appends are unlocked `O_APPEND` writes, while `_trim` reads the file and `atomic_write`s a prefix under `locked`. Two overlapping samples: A reads the log for trim, B appends a newer row, A rewrites without B’s row. That sample is gone, so a later sum over the log undercounts the interval that row covered.
chunk_findings.title: `record` / `_trim`

chunk_findings.detail: A transcript whose assistant lines do not parse is reported as a measured zero. Given one `*.jsonl` touched after `since` whose only line contains `"assistant"` but is truncated so `json.loads` raises, `_scan` increments `skipped` and adds neither a row nor a bare turn. `_tokens` then sees total 0 and unmetered 0 and returns `OK` 0.0, with the parse failure only in `detail["skipped"]`. That is a false zero: the file was not readable as usage, so the reading must be UNAVAILABLE.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters_local.py:136

chunk_findings.detail: Dedup keeps the first timestamp and the max counts, so a completed turn can fall out of the window and be counted as zero. Given the same `(message.id, requestId)` twice in scan order — first line at T−10s with `input_tokens=1`, second at T+5s with `input_tokens=500` — `_merged` stores `at=T−10` and tokens 500. For a window starting at T, `read_claude_tokens` drops that row (`r.at >= start` fails) and, with no other turns, returns `OK` 0.0. The code’s own partial-line case is exactly this order, so the finished usage is an undercount.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters_local.py:88

chunk_findings.detail: Session starts with an unusable time are dropped and can become a measured zero. Given `ctx.events` holding one `session.started` whose `ts` `clock.epoch` cannot parse (`default=-1.0`), the filter `-1.0 >= start` excludes it, `inside` is empty, and the reading is `OK` 0.0 with no unmetered count. The source was read and a start exists; zero claims nothing started.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters_local.py:315

chunk_findings.detail: `snapshot_stream_line` treats any non-empty `unifiedWindows` object as the only source for that window. Given `{"type":"rate_limit_event","rate_limit_info":{"rateLimitType":"five_hour","utilization":0.42,"resetsAt":1700000000,"unifiedWindows":{"five_hour":{"resetsAt":1700000000}}}}`, `rows["five_hour"]` is truthy, the top-level 0.42 is ignored, `B.percent` on the window object is missing, and `_write` stores nothing. A real 42% figure is dropped (undercount / stale prior snapshot), which violates the function’s own “unifiedWindows or the single rateLimitType utilization” rule.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters_vendor.py:212

chunk_findings.detail: `_trim` reads the entire sample log into memory via `.read_text()` and `.splitlines()`, then serializes and writes back the tail. Given an input sample log that grows very large (e.g., exceeding `samples_max_bytes` significantly due to bursts or slower trim intervals), loading the entire file into memory can cause excessive memory consumption or OOM conditions.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters.py:80

chunk_findings.detail: `read_all` turns a thrown reader into `unavailable(name, "", "", "", reason, ctx.now)`. `best` only keeps rows whose `window` and `unit` equal the caller's query, so that placeholder never matches. Given a Claude token reader that raises `OSError` while covering `window="5h"` / `unit="tokens"`, `best(readings, "5h", "tokens")` returns `None` (no reader) instead of UNAVAILABLE. A caller that treats `None` as no spend records a false zero and violates r-no-silent-cost.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters.py:51

chunk_findings.detail: `record` appends with `O_APPEND` and no `locked()`, then `_trim` replaces the path via `atomic_write`. A second `record` that opens the inode before the rename writes into the unlinked file and is dropped. Two overlapping samples of a file already over `samples_max_bytes` leave the log without one of the rows, so a later read of the sample log undercounts.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters.py:90

chunk_findings.detail: Duplicate transcript turns are merged with max token counts but the timestamp is always the first line scanned. Given the same `(message.id, requestId)` in two jsonl files, first seen at t=90 with 10 tokens and later at t=110 with 50 tokens, the stored row stays at 90 with 50 tokens. A window that starts at 100 then drops the turn (`r.at >= start` fails), so those tokens are a silent undercount for the window they actually fell in, and an overcount for any window that still includes 90.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters_local.py:_merged

chunk_findings.detail: Session events whose timestamps cannot be parsed are treated as before every window. `clock.epoch(e.ts, default=-1.0) >= start` excludes them, and nothing records them as unmetered. Input: one `session.started` event with `ts=""` (or any value `clock.epoch` cannot parse) and a window start of 0. The reader returns OK 0.0. That is a false zero: the log was not empty, the count could not be taken, and the reading is not UNAVAILABLE.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters_local.py:read_ddflow_sessions

chunk_findings.detail: `best` treats every empty-window UNAVAILABLE as covering the query, but the filter ignores unit and harness. Given readings `[unavailable(source="claude-cache", window="", unit="percent", reason="cache unreadable"), ok(source="transcript", window="session", unit="tokens", value=100)]`, `best(..., "5h", "tokens")` has an empty match and returns the percent-cache failure. Nothing failed for 5h tokens and no reader covers that window; the result should be None, not a Claude cache outage. The same input with `harness="kilo"` still returns the Claude failure.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters.py:73

data.body: services/suitelock.state_dir, services/lanes/capacity.slot_dir, services/selfupgrade._state and services/meters_base.state_dir each repeat base = XDG_STATE_HOME or [REDACTED:path], then append their own subdirectory. Move the base lookup to one function and have the four call it. Acceptance: one definition of the lookup; each caller's resolved path is unchanged, by test. Found by B-quota-meters at its dedupe gate.
data.title: One helper for the user state directory: four services repeat the XDG_STATE_HOME lookup

chunk_findings.detail: The `_subset` validator accepts a list with duplicate entries: `ok = isinstance(value, list) and bool(value) and all(v in allowed for v in value)` never checks `len(value) == len(set(value))`. Given a config `token_fields = ["input", "input"]`, validation passes, but the meter that sums token kinds will add the input token count twice, producing an inflated usage total (or for duplicate `token_windows`, duplicate windows in a downstream accumulation). This is a concrete input that makes the reading wrong: the configured selection no longer represents "which token kinds a reading's total includes" as it does for a unique list, and the check intended to enforce `_subset` fails to prevent it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/quota.py:_subset (also affects token_fields at ~line 82)

chunk_findings.detail: `record` appends to `ctx.samples` without acquiring `locked(ctx.samples)`, while `_trim` takes that lock and replaces the whole file. Interleaving: process A is in `_trim`, has read the old log, and is about to `atomic_write`; process B enters `record`, opens the old `ctx.samples` with `O_APPEND` and writes a new sample; A then renames the trimmed file over the path without B's row. B's sample is silently dropped from the sample log, producing an undercount. The lock is ineffective because only one of the two writers honors it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters.py:record/_trim

chunk_findings.detail: When a registered reader raises, `read_all` appends `B.unavailable(name, "", "", "", reason, ctx.now)` with empty `window`, `unit`, and `harness`. `best` matches only the exact requested `window`/`unit`/`harness`, so for any concrete metric request the failed reader normally covers, that unavailable reading is filtered out and `best` returns `None` even though a reader did run and did cover the metric. `best`'s own contract says `None` means no reader covers it at all; a caller that treats `None` as absence and shows 0 then converts an unreadable meter into a false zero, violating r-no-silent-cost.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters.py:read_all/best

chunk_findings.detail: `is_number` calls `math.isfinite(value)` directly on any `int`, and Python raises `OverflowError` for Python integers larger than the float range, e.g. `is_number(10**400)`. A truthful large token count in `Reading(..., status="ok", value=10**400)` or an out-of-range percent `percent(10**400, 1.0)` therefore crashes the meter read instead of returning an ok reading or refusing the unusable figure as `None`/UNAVAILABLE. This violates the “cannot be taken is UNAVAILABLE, never zero” path by raising on input that should be handled as a non-percent or upheld as a real Python integer.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters_base.py:25

chunk_findings.detail: A truncated/invalid JSON assistant line increments `usage.skipped` but never enters `usage.unmetered`, and `read_claude_tokens` passes `skipped` only as detail. Given a single touched transcript containing one torn assistant line such as `{"type":"assistant", "message":{"usage":{"input_tokens":5`, `transcript_usage` returns `rows=[]`, `unmetered=[]`, `skipped=1`, so `_tokens` sees `total=0` and `unmetered=0` and returns an OK zero token reading. That is a false zero for a turn that was present but could not be read, violating r-no-silent-cost.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters_local.py:_scan / read_claude_tokens / _tokens

chunk_findings.detail: `_breakdown` converts `None` optional token kinds to `0` with `getattr(r, kind) or 0`. If `ctx.token_fields` selects an optional kind such as `cache_read`, and a transcript turn has only `input_tokens` and `output_tokens` (so `TokenRow.cache_read is None`), this turn is not counted in `unmetered`; `_tokens` returns OK 0 for that selected kind. The absent kind means no usable figure and must be unmetered/unavailable, not zero—the module’s own `TokenRow` doc says an exposed-absent kind is `None`, never `0`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters_local.py:_breakdown / _tokens

chunk_findings.detail: For Anthropic transcripts, `usage.input_tokens` is the total input count, and `cache_read_input_tokens`/`cache_creation_input_tokens` are subsets of that total. `_row_of` stores the total as `input` and also stores the cache subsets, and `_tokens` sums every selected field. With the normal `token_fields` set containing `input`, `cache_read`, and `cache_write`, a turn with `input_tokens=100`, `output_tokens=50`, `cache_read_input_tokens=30`, `cache_creation_input_tokens=20` returns 200 tokens instead of 150, a clear overcount.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters_local.py:_tokens / _breakdown

chunk_findings.detail: A `session.started` event whose `e.ts` is malformed is turned into `-1.0` by `clock.epoch(e.ts, default=-1.0)` and then filtered out by `>= start`, so it disappears from every window without being recorded as unmetered. Given one malformed `session.started` event and no valid events, `read_ddflow_sessions` returns an OK reading of `0` sessions rather than `UNAVAILABLE`, even though the log contains a session start that cannot be placed in a window. This is a false zero/undercount.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters_local.py:read_ddflow_sessions

chunk_findings.detail: `cachedUsageUtilization.utilization.<window>.utilization` in `[REDACTED:path]` is a fraction 0-1, not a percent 0-100. With `CACHE_SCALE = 1.0`, a concrete cache like `{"cachedUsageUtilization":{"fetchedAtMs":1729591714382,"accountUuid":"u","utilization":{"five_hour":{"utilization":0.5,"resets_at":"2024-10-22T11:00:00Z"}}}}` produces a reading of `0.5` percent instead of `50.0` percent. This is a 100x undercount for real usage, directly against the “no false zero or undercount” intent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters_vendor.py: CACHE_SCALE / read_claude_cache

chunk_findings.detail: `write_cache` writes `path` without creating its parent directory. The `ctx` helper sets `snapshot` to `tmp / "state" / "vendor.json"` but never creates `tmp/state`, so a natural test setup such as `write_cache(ctx(tmp_path).snapshot, five=50, week=20)` raises `FileNotFoundError` before any meter code runs. The function should create `path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` like `write_transcript` does.
chunk_findings.title: tests/quota_meters_support.py:46

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `assert all(r.status == MB.UNAVAILABLE for r in V.read_claude_cache(ctx(tmp_path)))` is vacuously true when `read_claude_cache` returns an empty list. With this `tmp_path` where no cache file exists, an implementation that returned `[]` would still pass while producing no `UNAVAILABLE` reading for the configured `5h`/`week` windows—the exact silent-cost absence this suite is intended to prevent. The test should assert the returned window set is `{"5h", "week"}` with `UNAVAILABLE`, as the malformed-file test does; the same vacuous `all(...)` form appears for absent/corrupt snapshots in `TestSnapshot.test_no_rate_limits_writes_nothing_never_zero` and `TestSnapshot.test_corrupt_snapshot_is_unavailable_and_a_new_write_heals_it`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_quota_meters.py:test_missing_file_is_unavailable

chunk_findings.detail: `turn()` defaults its transcript row timestamp to the current time (`NOW`), as shown by every other test in this file that calls `turn()` without `at` and expects the row to be counted in the 5h window. This test then sets only the file `mtime` to `NOW - 200 * HOUR`. The file is old by mtime, but the row it contains has an in-window timestamp, so a correct reader that honors the row timestamp would report 116 tokens, not 0. The test asserts `(MB.OK, 0.0)`, blessing a false zero/undercount for a transcript file whose mtime diverges from its row timestamp (for example after copy preserving an old mtime or a clock adjustment). If the implementation ever trusts the row timestamp over mtime, this test fails; as written it locks in the silent undercount that r-no-silent-cost says must not happen.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_quota_meters_local.py:test_transcripts_with_nothing_in_the_window_measure_zero

chunk_findings.detail: A reader that raises is turned into one UNAVAILABLE reading with blank window, unit and harness (`unavailable(name, "", "", "", reason, ctx.now)`). `best` only matches on those three fields, so given Claude token reads raising `OSError` and a caller asking `best(read_all(ctx), "5h", "tokens", "claude")`, the failure row never matches and `best` returns None (“no reader covers it”) instead of UNAVAILABLE. A caller that treats None as no usage records a false zero, which is the silent-cost case this wrapper is supposed to prevent.
chunk_findings.title: `best` / `read_all`

chunk_findings.detail: Appends are unlocked `O_APPEND` writes, while `_trim` reads the file and `atomic_write`s a prefix under `locked`. Two overlapping samples: A reads the log for trim, B appends a newer row, A rewrites without B’s row. That sample is gone, so a later sum over the log undercounts the interval that row covered.
chunk_findings.title: `record` / `_trim`

chunk_findings.detail: A transcript whose assistant lines do not parse is reported as a measured zero. Given one `*.jsonl` touched after `since` whose only line contains `"assistant"` but is truncated so `json.loads` raises, `_scan` increments `skipped` and adds neither a row nor a bare turn. `_tokens` then sees total 0 and unmetered 0 and returns `OK` 0.0, with the parse failure only in `detail["skipped"]`. That is a false zero: the file was not readable as usage, so the reading must be UNAVAILABLE.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters_local.py:136

chunk_findings.detail: Dedup keeps the first timestamp and the max counts, so a completed turn can fall out of the window and be counted as zero. Given the same `(message.id, requestId)` twice in scan order — first line at T−10s with `input_tokens=1`, second at T+5s with `input_tokens=500` — `_merged` stores `at=T−10` and tokens 500. For a window starting at T, `read_claude_tokens` drops that row (`r.at >= start` fails) and, with no other turns, returns `OK` 0.0. The code’s own partial-line case is exactly this order, so the finished usage is an undercount.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters_local.py:88

chunk_findings.detail: Session starts with an unusable time are dropped and can become a measured zero. Given `ctx.events` holding one `session.started` whose `ts` `clock.epoch` cannot parse (`default=-1.0`), the filter `-1.0 >= start` excludes it, `inside` is empty, and the reading is `OK` 0.0 with no unmetered count. The source was read and a start exists; zero claims nothing started.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters_local.py:315

chunk_findings.detail: `snapshot_stream_line` treats any non-empty `unifiedWindows` object as the only source for that window. Given `{"type":"rate_limit_event","rate_limit_info":{"rateLimitType":"five_hour","utilization":0.42,"resetsAt":1700000000,"unifiedWindows":{"five_hour":{"resetsAt":1700000000}}}}`, `rows["five_hour"]` is truthy, the top-level 0.42 is ignored, `B.percent` on the window object is missing, and `_write` stores nothing. A real 42% figure is dropped (undercount / stale prior snapshot), which violates the function’s own “unifiedWindows or the single rateLimitType utilization” rule.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters_vendor.py:212

chunk_findings.detail: The torn-line fix is incomplete because `_scan` still pre-filters with `if '"assistant"' not in line: continue`. Given a transcript whose only recent line is the torn prefix `{"type":"ass` — the beginning of `{"type":"assistant","message":{"usage": ...}` — the line does not contain the exact double-quoted substring `"assistant"`, so `_scan` skips it before `json.loads` ever sees it and never inserts `bare[(str(path), n)] = None`. The transcript has one touched file with an unreadable possible assistant turn, yet `usage.unmetered` remains empty, `gaps` is 0, `_tokens` sees `unmetered=0`, and `read_claude_tokens` returns `OK 0.0`. Previous finding #5 is therefore still reachable by truncating before the sentinel rather than after it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters_local.py:_scan

chunk_findings.detail: `none_of` is meant to reject an empty set of readings, but `bool(readings)` is True for any iterator/generator even when it is empty. Concrete input: `none_of(iter([]))` evaluates to `True` because `bool(iter([]))` is `True` and `all(...)` over the empty iterator is `True`. That recreates the vacuous assertion this helper was added to prevent whenever a caller passes a generator expression or iterator instead of a concrete list, allowing a meter that returns no readings to be treated as “all unavailable” and pass.
chunk_findings.title: tests/quota_meters_support.py:125

chunk_findings.detail: The fix only swaps `all(...)` for `none_of(got)`; the test still does not assert the returned window set is `{"5h","week"}`. A `read_claude_cache` that, on a missing cache file, returns just one `UNAVAILABLE` reading for `"week"` (or omits `"5h"`) makes the assertion pass because `none_of` only checks that there is at least one reading and that each is unavailable. That is exactly the silent missing-window undercount this test is meant to prevent, so the window-set half of the previous finding is not answered by this probe.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_quota_meters.py::test_missing_file_is_unavailable

chunk_findings.detail: The new test does not exercise the reported race. It only asserts that `record` called `M.locked(c.samples)` once; it never starts a concurrent `_trim`, and it never verifies that the append actually occurs inside that lock. A faulty `record` that does `with locked(ctx.samples): pass` and then appends outside the lock would satisfy `held == [c.samples]`, yet the original HIGH interleaving—A reads the old log, B appends a new row, A renames over it—would still drop B’s row and undercount. The confirmed finding is therefore not answered by this probe.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_quota_meters.py:349 test_a_trim_does_not_lose_a_row_appended_beside_it

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 12 still holds: the change only makes the row timestamp as old as the file mtime so the fixture no longer contradicts the mtime prefilter; it does not remove the prefilter. A transcript file with an in-window row but an older mtime is still skipped. Concrete input: `write_transcript(c.claude_projects / "p" / "a.jsonl", [turn(at=NOW)], mtime=NOW - 6 * HOUR)` (as with a copied/restored file preserving an older mtime). The meter skips the file by mtime before reading the in-window row, so `_tokens(c)` returns `OK 0` despite a row whose timestamp is inside the window. This change adjusts the test to agree with the bug rather than fixing the false zero.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_quota_meters_local.py:85

chunk_findings.detail: `_trim` reads the entire sample log into memory via `.read_text()` and `.splitlines()`, then serializes and writes back the tail. Given an input sample log that grows very large (e.g., exceeding `samples_max_bytes` significantly due to bursts or slower trim intervals), loading the entire file into memory can cause excessive memory consumption or OOM conditions.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters.py:80

chunk_findings.detail: `read_all` turns a thrown reader into `unavailable(name, "", "", "", reason, ctx.now)`. `best` only keeps rows whose `window` and `unit` equal the caller's query, so that placeholder never matches. Given a Claude token reader that raises `OSError` while covering `window="5h"` / `unit="tokens"`, `best(readings, "5h", "tokens")` returns `None` (no reader) instead of UNAVAILABLE. A caller that treats `None` as no spend records a false zero and violates r-no-silent-cost.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters.py:51

chunk_findings.detail: `record` appends with `O_APPEND` and no `locked()`, then `_trim` replaces the path via `atomic_write`. A second `record` that opens the inode before the rename writes into the unlinked file and is dropped. Two overlapping samples of a file already over `samples_max_bytes` leave the log without one of the rows, so a later read of the sample log undercounts.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters.py:90

chunk_findings.detail: Duplicate transcript turns are merged with max token counts but the timestamp is always the first line scanned. Given the same `(message.id, requestId)` in two jsonl files, first seen at t=90 with 10 tokens and later at t=110 with 50 tokens, the stored row stays at 90 with 50 tokens. A window that starts at 100 then drops the turn (`r.at >= start` fails), so those tokens are a silent undercount for the window they actually fell in, and an overcount for any window that still includes 90.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters_local.py:_merged

chunk_findings.detail: Session events whose timestamps cannot be parsed are treated as before every window. `clock.epoch(e.ts, default=-1.0) >= start` excludes them, and nothing records them as unmetered. Input: one `session.started` event with `ts=""` (or any value `clock.epoch` cannot parse) and a window start of 0. The reader returns OK 0.0. That is a false zero: the log was not empty, the count could not be taken, and the reading is not UNAVAILABLE.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters_local.py:read_ddflow_sessions

chunk_findings.detail: `best` treats every empty-window UNAVAILABLE as covering the query, but the filter ignores unit and harness. Given readings `[unavailable(source="claude-cache", window="", unit="percent", reason="cache unreadable"), ok(source="transcript", window="session", unit="tokens", value=100)]`, `best(..., "5h", "tokens")` has an empty match and returns the percent-cache failure. Nothing failed for 5h tokens and no reader covers that window; the result should be None, not a Claude cache outage. The same input with `harness="kilo"` still returns the Claude failure.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters.py:73

chunk_findings.detail: `is_number(10**400)` now returns `False` because `math.isfinite(10**400)` raises `OverflowError`, and the `except` suppresses it. `10**400` is a finite real number, so callers using this predicate to decide whether a measured quantity is countable will treat a valid, finite reading as “not a number” and drop it. In a sample log containing only a token count of `10**400`, that row/reading is skipped and the later total becomes `0` instead of counting it or reporting the reading as UNAVAILABLE; treating a huge finite count as absent is an undercount/false zero.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters_base.py:is_number

chunk_findings.detail: A torn final line is only recorded as unmetered if it first passes `if '"assistant"' not in line: continue`. If a transcript file being written ends with a partial assistant event truncated before that literal appears, for example file content `{"type":"ass` with no trailing newline, `_scan` sees a line that is not valid JSON and contains no `"assistant"` substring; it executes `continue` and never adds `bare[(str(path), n)] = None`. Then `usage.unmetered` is empty and `_reading` returns a zero-token reading with `unmetered=0` for a turn that could not be counted, a false zero/undercount.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/meters_local.py:_scan

chunk_findings.detail: The change replaces `assert got and all(r.status == MB.UNAVAILABLE and r.value is None for r in got)` with `assert none_of(got)`. The old expression explicitly required `got` to be non-empty; the new `none_of` predicate, as used to replace the repeated `all(...)` checks, is true for an empty sequence. So if `M.read_all(ctx(tmp_path))` ever returns `[]` for an environment with no readable state—e.g. when the configured reader list is empty or a regression drops all unavailable rows—this test still passes, and a false zero “no spend” can go undetected. That undercuts the very false-zero protection this test existed to provide.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_quota_meters.py:test_nothing_readable_gives_no_number_at_all

chunk_findings.detail: This regression test does not reproduce the confirmed append-vs-trim race it is named for. It records one row far below `samples_max_bytes=2000`, never starts a second overlapping `record`, never creates a file that is already over the bound, and asserts only that `M.locked` was called with `c.samples`. Given an implementation where `_trim` still replaces the file without taking the same lock, this test passes while two overlapping samples of an already-over-bound file still drop one row and a later `_rows(c)` undercounts. The probe therefore does not answer the previous race finding.

chunk_findings.detail: A torn assistant record is only marked unmetered when the flushed bytes already contain the substring `"assistant"`. `_scan` still does `if '"assistant"' not in line: continue` before `json.loads`, so a truncated last line never reaches `bare[(str(path), n)] = None`. Given a transcript whose only line is `{"parentUuid":"aaaaaaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-eeeeeeeeeeee","isSidechain":false,"type":"assis` (Claude field order, cut before the type value is complete), the line is dropped, `usage.unmetered` stays empty, and the window total is an OK 0. That is a false zero: the file was not empty and the turn was not counted.

data.body: A delta round prints its findings as #1..#5, but the gate numbers them cumulatively (#19..#23). `ddflow review triage --finding 5 --refuted` therefore silently re-verdicted an old CONFIRMED HIGH finding from round one to REFUTED, and the summary still showed 5 untriaged. Seen on B-quota-meters, corrected by hand. Wanted: the delta output prints the gate's numbers or digests; triage of a finding that already has a verdict refuses unless told to replace it, and names the old verdict. Acceptance: a test where re-triage with a different verdict exits 3, and one where a delta's printed number triages that delta's finding.
data.title: review triage overwrites an already triaged finding with no warning; numbers run across rounds, the printed #N from a delta do not
